2608.26609.title: Thermally quenched metastability in metal-insulator transitions via elemental substitution
2608.26609.summary:
- Rapid cooling (>10⁹ K s⁻¹) suppresses the VO₂ metal‑insulator transition when tungsten is substituted, trapping a long‑lived metallic phase.
- Relaxation follows nucleation‑dominated kinetics with a thermally activated barrier introduced by W.
- Elemental substitution thus provides a route to thermally quenched metastability in electronic phase transitions.

2608.26751.title: Interlayer-engineering of Charge Order Wave Vector in Kagome Metals
2608.26751.summary:
- Interlayer coupling tunes CsV₃Sb₅ from a 4×1 charge order in the monolayer to a 2×2 order in the bulk.
- Monolayer phonons show instability at q = (¼, 0, ; increasing interlayer spacing softens the M‑point phonon, triggering the bulk 2×2 instability.
- The study unifies surface‑observed 4×1 and bulk‑observed 2×2 charge orders as competing tendencies controlled by dimensionality.

2608.27134.title: 3D- (H-theta-phi) magnetic phase diagram of antiferromagnetic metal GdB6 with electron and lattice instability
2608.27134.summary:
- GdB6 exhibits static Jahn‑Teller distortions and dynamic charge stripes, producing anisotropic charge transport.
- Two antiferromagnetic phases (AF I, AF II) form an impeller‑shaped H–φ phase diagram in the (and (planes.
- A 5d spin‑density wave and stripe‑induced RKKY suppression generate the observed anisotropy and phase boundaries.

2608.27200.title: Multi-orbital physics in inverse Lieb lattice altermagnets
2608.27200.summary:
- Developed symmetry‑based microscopic Hamiltonian for inverse Lieb lattice altermagnets, incorporating sublattice and orbital degrees of freedom.
- Applied to vanadium oxychalcogenides: \(xy\) orbitals stabilize altermagnetism; Hund’s coupling induces \(xz/yz\) orbital order.
- Multi‑orbital models uncover orbital‑selective topological edge states.

2608.27411.title: A continuous confinement-deconfinement transition in a triangular quantum magnet
2608.27411.summary:
- Continuous confinement–deconfinement transition in TlYbS₂: antiferromagnetic order below 53 K gives way to a gapless spin‑liquid with a spinon Fermi surface at μ₀H_c≈3 T.
- Signatures: finite residual κ/T, Pauli‑like susceptibility, T‑independent NMR Knight shift, and enhanced scattering rate without critical density‑of‑states growth.
- Indicates a quantum critical point governed by fractionalized excitations beyond the Ginzburg–Landau paradigm.

cond-mat/0401304.title: Quantum-magneto oscillations in a supramolecular Mn(II)-[3 x 3] grid
cond-mat/0401304.summary:
- High‑field torque magnetometry on Mn(II)-[3 × 3] grid reveals oscillatory torque vs. field above 5 T.
- Oscillations observed at 3 He temperatures, indicating quantum‑magneto effects.
- A theoretical model successfully reproduces the magneto‑oscillation behavior.

cond-mat/0401293.title: Ferromagnetism in Fe-doped SnO2 thin films
cond-mat/0401293.summary:
- Fe‑doped SnO₂ thin films are transparent ferromagnets with TC ≈ 610 K and Ms ≈ 2 Am²/kg.
- Mossbauer spectra reveal high‑spin Fe³⁺; only ~23 % of Fe ions are magnetically ordered, each carrying ~8 µB.
- Ferromagnetism attributed to Fe³⁺ coupling through an electron trapped in an oxygen vacancy (F‑center).

cond-mat/0401296.title: Ultrafast Conductivity Dynamics in Pentacene Probed using Terahertz Spectroscopy
cond-mat/0401296.summary:
- Measured picosecond photoconductivity in pentacene crystals via optical‑pump THz‑probe.
- Mobility drops from ~4 cm²/Vs at 30 K to ~2 cm²/Vs at room temperature.
- THz signal indicates rapid (< ps) trapping of photoexcited carriers, likely by excitons, polarons, or impurities.

cond-mat/0401292.title: Phases of a rotating Bose-Einstein condensate with anharmonic confinement
cond-mat/0401292.summary:
- Identified three phases (multiple, single, mixed quantization) in a rotating BEC with quadratic‑plus‑quartic confinement.
- Derived a universal phase diagram; continuous transitions exact for weak coupling and small anharmonicity.
- Variational predictions agree with Gross‑Pitaevskii numerical solutions.

cond-mat/0401280.title: Observation of narrow fluorescence from doubly driven four-level atoms at room temperature
cond-mat/0401280.summary:
- Narrow fluorescence peaks appear in Rb‑85 under dual‑laser 3D molasses; one laser fixed detuned from cooling transition, the other scanned over repumping lines.
- Peaks form symmetric pairs whose separation increases with cooling‑laser detuning; large detunings yield additional small peaks.
- A simple model explains the observed spectral features.

cond-mat/0401279.title: Fluorescence from doubly driven four-level atoms - A density matrix approach
cond-mat/0401279.summary:
- Four‑level density‑matrix model reproduces narrow Rb‑85 fluorescence peaks under cooling and repumper lasers.
- Quantum interference alters probe‑induced population transfer, sharpening double‑resonance velocity selection.
- Co‑ and counter‑propagating beam geometry yields narrow fluorescence peaks in a room‑temperature thermal gas.

quant-ph/0401089.title: Optical conductivity of small adiabatic polarons with a long-range electron-phonon interaction
quant-ph/0401089.summary:
- Calculated optical conductivity and effective mass of small adiabatic Fröhlich polarons at zero temperature.
- Compared results with small adiabatic Holstein polarons, highlighting differences due to long‑range electron‑phonon coupling.
- Modeled ions as isotropic 3D oscillators to analyze electron hopping and optical absorption.

cond-mat/0401267.title: A first principles simulation of rigid water
cond-mat/0401267.summary:
- CP simulations of water with rigid molecules use larger time steps, enabling longer time scales.
- Structural properties and diffusion coefficients from the rigid model match experiments better than flexible simulations.
- The approach paves the way for ab initio studies of aqueous solutions (e.g., hydrophobic solvation) beyond current time‑scale limits.

cond-mat/0401232.title: Origin of asymmetric reversal modes in ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic multilayers
cond-mat/0401232.summary:
- Asymmetric reversal modes appear in certain exchange‑bias multilayers.
- Domain‑state simulations show the effect depends on the angle between the AFM easy axis and the applied field.
- At specific angles the FM reverses symmetrically via coherent rotation; at others it reverses asymmetrically, sometimes producing zero perpendicular magnetization.

cond-mat/0401212.title: Vortex waves and the onset of turbulence in $^3$He-B
cond-mat/0401212.summary:
- Finne et al. identified the intrinsic turbulence onset criterion \(q=\alpha/(1-\alpha')<1\) in \(^{3}\)He‑B.
- The criterion corresponds to marginally damped Kelvin waves; for \(q>1\) waves cannot grow to trigger reconnections.
- Analysis of rotating‑superfluid modes confirms \(q=1\) as the crossover between damped and propagating Kelvin waves in the long‑wavelength limit.

2608.27457.title: Spectral Fingerprints of Gauge Theories on a Quantum Computer
2608.27457.summary:
- Unbiased maximally mixed state spectral sampling extracts finite‑resolution spectra across the entire energy range of a Hamiltonian.
- Applied to a (1+d SO(gauge theory, the algorithm runs on near‑term superconducting hardware with 78 two‑qubit‑gate depth and halves qubit count via dynamical circuits.
- Introduces Pauli‑frame compilation for controlled‑time evolution, trivial readout‑error mitigation, and post‑processing for disordered transitions and mid‑spectrum density of states.

2608.27453.title: Metallogenic quantum criticality: Fermi surface nucleation at transitions between gapped phases
2608.27453.summary:
- MGQCP: a quantum critical point where a full Fermi surface emerges between two fully gapped insulators, breaking the usual isolated‑point gaplessness rule.
- Effective field theory for transitions between distinct fractional Chern insulators shows conformal transport scaling yet a non‑Fermi‑liquid electron spectral function.
- Minimal microscopic realization: a periodically modulated quantum Hall bilayer, with implications for tunable Chern bands in moiré materials.

2608.27446.title: Exact Stiffness and Dynamical Responses from Fock-Space Fragmentation
2608.27446.summary:
- QGN models show Fock‑space fragmentation: excitations split into Krylov subspaces with fixed particle‑hole number, giving dynamically invariant sectors.
- The stiffness of the broken continuous symmetry equals its variational Gaussian value; a phase twist couples only to the one‑particle–one‑hole fragment, making the variational curvature exact.
- Perturbations staying within a fixed fragment yield exact response functions (susceptibility, conductivity, structure factors, Green’s functions) from the corresponding few‑body sector.

2608.27445.title: Band's Geometry Origin of Quantum Spin Transport Phenomena
2608.27445.summary:
- Geometric framework links band/Fermi‑surface structure to spin‑dependent transport.
- Hyperbolic constant‑energy regions generate a Fermi‑velocity term that drives spin currents.
- Time‑reversal symmetry maps spin operators to the band’s exterior algebra, enabling a symplectic/contact‑geometric description of spin‑separated transport.

2608.27228.title: 2-Morita Theory of $E_2$-Algebras and Module Categories
2608.27228.summary:
- Introduces $n$‑Morita categories $\mathrm{Mrt}_{E_n}(\mathcal{C})$ to unify $n$‑Morita equivalence for $E_n$‑algebras and topological orders.
- Proves for $n=1,2$ that the functor $\mathrm{Mod}_n$ is an equivalence, linking algebraic higher Morita theory with module‑category realizations.
- Uses bi‑bimodules and orientation data to describe local and confined modules, clarifying defect fusion rules from condensation.

2608.26954.title: Decoupled domain-texture switching from magnetic easy axis in kagome ferromagnet EuTi3Bi4
2608.26954.summary:
- Domain orientation in EuTi₃Bi₄ switches between a‑ and b‑axes with temperature or an out‑of‑plane field, despite a fixed c‑axis easy magnetization.
- Switching arises from competing in‑plane anisotropies: single‑ion anisotropy favors a‑axis, while nearest‑neighbor anisotropic exchange favors b‑axis.
- Exfoliated flakes raise the critical switching temperature, demonstrating tunable texture control via in‑plane interaction balance.

2608.27519.title: Exact branch-transfer criterion for common-mode Thomson heat cancellation in thermoelectric couples
2608.27519.summary:
- Exact branch‑transfer criterion: common‑mode Thomson heat cancels iff the differential thermopower measures of the p‑ and n‑branches are equal.
- In the linear‑common‑mode limit, matching \(R_i/K_i^{\text{leg}}\) suffices for cancellation, even with non‑identical legs.
- Derived array law for split thermal pads: \(\Delta Q_{c,\Sigma}=\sum_j C_j I_j \Delta T_{c,j}\); for series elements with isothermal hot pairs, \(I\Delta V_\Sigma=-\Delta Q_{c,\Sigma}\).

2608.27520.title: Asphericity Lifts the Degeneracy Among Ordering Mechanisms on Curved Surfaces
2608.27520.summary:
- Spherical surfaces hide the signature of different ordering mechanisms; asphericity lifts this degeneracy.
- On an ellipsoid, mechanisms separate into distinct powers of the distance to the tangent plane, readable from the structure‑factor quadrupole and radius of gyration.
- Riesz s‑energy shows a sharp transition at a marginal power, while screened Coulomb potential lets ionic strength continuously tune the exponent, enabling experimental control of the conductor‑to‑packing crossover.

2608.27533.title: Ab initio Modeling of MoS2/Oxide Device Interfaces with Machine Learned Electronic Structures
2608.27533.summary:
- ML‑electronic structure + QT solver gives 10,000× speedup for >20k‑atom MoS₂/oxide devices.
- Explicit HfO₂/Al₂O₃ oxides modeled in transport domain for single‑layer MoS₂ FETs.
- Undercoordinated Hf/Al atoms at the interface strongly modify current magnitude and propagation.

2608.27552.title: Collinear altermagnetism for 3D chiral higher-order topological insulators
2608.27552.summary:
- Altermagnetism on a Lieb lattice combined with a 3D TI produces a chiral \(C_4\mathcal{T}\)-protected higher‑order topological insulator.
- The collinear \(d\)-wave magnetism shifts and gaps surface Dirac cones, yielding chiral hinge channels.
- Candidate material classes are identified, demonstrating altermagnetism as a viable route to intrinsic chiral HOTIs.

2608.27572.title: Scale-free correlations in extremely persistent active matter
2608.27572.summary:
- Demonstrates algebraic decay of density and swim‑velocity correlations as \(r^{-(d+}\) (with log corrections in 2D) for infinitely persistent active Brownian particles at low density and small swim velocity.
- Finds corresponding cusps at \(k=0\) in reciprocal space, confirming scale‑free behavior.
- Validates analytical predictions with numerical simulations.

2608.27587.title: Compiling Chemical Knowledge into Executable Descriptors for Materials Prediction
2608.27587.summary:
- CRISP generates, consolidates, and compiles chemical rules into scalar descriptors using a language‑model, without requiring labeled data.
- For inorganic‑crystal synthesizability, CRISP outperforms expert‑curated and generic representations and surpasses specialized models, especially under domain shifts.
- The same workflow yields competitive descriptors for formation energy and ionic conductivity, revealing task‑specific limits for shear modulus and offering a dataset‑blind, auditable knowledge‑to‑representation pipeline.

2608.27588.title: Topological signatures in the quench dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems
2608.27588.summary:
- Quench of graphene by circularly polarized light produces a period‑averaged edge bond current that oscillates around a dc value, signaling an induced topological phase.
- In an isolated ribbon the dc current equals Floquet band currents weighted by their occupations; coupling to a fermionic bath causes the current and conductance to rise then saturate to a nonequilibrium steady state.
- In the weak‑coupling limit the summed conductance is quantized, revealing the number of edge modes at the zero‑quasienergy and Floquet‑zone‑boundary gaps, confirmed by two‑terminal transport in a finite‑size model.

2608.27589.title: Atomistic Indicators of the Ductile-to-Brittle Transition in Polycrystalline Tungsten: Temperature and Rhenium Effects on Crack-Tip Plasticity
2608.27589.summary:
- Temperature lowers instability stress and stiffness in W, with a sigmoid crossover near 870 K under high‑rate loading.
- 10 % Re increases pre‑instability plasticity and work accumulation, modifying dislocation pathways instead of merely strengthening.
- Re alters retained ½<111> line character and the timing of near‑tip dislocation activity, offering atomistic markers of the ductile‑to‑brittle transition.

2608.27590.title: Physics-informed learning for the inverse problem in resonant ultrasound spectroscopy
2608.27590.summary:
- Physics‑informed learning transforms the resonant‑ultrasound inverse problem into a constrained regression on a low‑dimensional manifold of admissible elasticity tensors.
- The method uses reduced spectral and geometric features (length, scale, aspect ratio, scale‑free spectral signatures, stability‑respecting ratios) to analytically recover full elastic constants.
- Benchmark results: MAE ≈ 20 GPa (C₁₁), 24 GPa (C₁₂), 2 GPa (C₄₄); MAPE 4–

2608.27625.title: Turning Zeeman splitting into switchable charge polarization in a double quantum dot
2608.27625.summary:
- Uniform Zeeman field can reverse the single‑electron charge polarization in an asymmetric double quantum dot.
- Two mechanisms: gate‑level asymmetry and unequal onsite interactions shift Zeeman‑shifted resonances relative to the reservoir chemical potential.
- Coulomb blockade keeps total occupation fixed, so the field induces spatial charge redistribution within the single‑electron sector.

2608.27917.title: Orbital-Selective Coexistence of Interlayer Spin-Singlet Formation and SDW Order with Anomalous Spin Reconfiguration in Bilayer Nickelate La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ Revealed by $^{17}$O-NMR
2608.27917.summary:
- SDW below 150 K: planar O(3,broaden, O(remains field‑free → commensurate stripe SDW with negligible spin on O(.
- Inner apical O(shows canceled internal field (antiparallel interlayer spins) but its signal disappears below ~115 K, indicating unstable interlayer

2608.28054.title: Spin-Selective Spectral Flattening and Wave-Packet Dynamics in a Flux-Engineered Lieb Lattice
2608.28054.summary:
- Spin‑dependent Peierls phases give ↑ and ↓ components effective fluxes α↑=½, α↓=0 in a Lieb lattice.
- At α0=αs=¼ the ↑ spectrum has two flat zero‑energy subbands, while ↓ remains dispersive, so full Aharonov–Bohm caging fails.
- Time evolution shows ↓ propagates freely, ↑ is strongly localized; reversing the flux swaps the slow/fast channels and the effect persists under moderate detuning.

2608.28119.title: Field-tuned quasiparticles and electronic structure in heavy-fermion YbNi4P2
2608.28119.summary:
- Quasiparticle masses in YbNi4P2 drop sharply with increasing magnetic field, matching single‑ion Kondo predictions.
- A Lifshitz transition at ~17 T produces abrupt changes in quantum‑oscillation frequencies, indicating a sudden Fermi‑surface/topology shift.
- The work demonstrates field‑tunable electronic structure in a heavy‑fermion system, guiding theoretical models of correlated electrons in high fields.

2608.28588.title: Interaction corrections to topological density three-point functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids: a coadjoint orbit perspective
2608.28588.summary:
- Interaction corrections to 2D Fermi liquid density three‑point functions are analyzed using a coadjoint‑orbit effective field theory.
- Generalized Landau interactions are mapped to bosonic tree diagrams, simplifying fermionic loop calculations.
- Even at linear order, a band‑curvature term \(\epsilon''(p_F)\) introduces a new nonanalytic structure, showing interactions alter topology‑sensitive correlations beyond the Galilean‑invariant case.

2608.27561.title: Pulling strings in real time: flux tube dynamics in (2+1)-d $\mathbb{Z}_2$-Higgs Gauge Theories
2608.27561.summary:
- Introduces Clifford‑augmented matrix product states (CAMPS) to simulate 2+1D ℤ₂ Higgs gauge theory at unprecedented volumes and timescales.
- Benchmarks flux‑tube statics and roughening against universal effective‑string theory, confirming spectral and entanglement predictions.
- Implements a real‑time string‑pull protocol that excites transverse modes, revealing collective dynamics and long‑lived confinement signatures.

2608.27767.title: Fractional Hall Conductance of Laughlin States from a Topological Index
2608.27767.summary:
- Rigorous Laughlin‑pump argument proving fractional Hall conductance as a topological index.
- Employs an index of a pair of pure states and infinite matrix‑product‑state analysis on a thin cylinder.
- Demonstrates Laughlin states represent topologically stable fractional quantum Hall phases.

2608.27861.title: Vectorized Symmetric and Fermionic Tensor Network Implementations for GPU-Accelerated Variational Monte Carlo
2608.27861.summary:
- Vectorized, block‑sparse tensor network formalism for symmetric/fermionic TNs enabling GPU‑accelerated amplitude evaluation.
- Batched tensor operations for abelian symmetric TNs, yielding up to 300× speedup over single‑core CPU on 2D Fermi–Hubbard VMC.
- GPU‑adapted TN‑VMC workflow that fully exploits GPU parallelism for ground‑state calculations of strongly correlated systems.

2608.28005.title: Projected q-Shells for Nested Gausslet Bases
2608.28005.summary:
- Introduces projected q‑shells (PQS) that restore two lost polynomial orders in nested gausslet bases.
- Shows PQS span is equivalent to an over‑complete overlapping‑patch basis, with minor loss from coordinate distortions.
- Achieves lower one‑electron and interaction errors for small molecules (e.g., H₂⁺, H₂, C₂) than standard nesting.

2608.28107.title: Charge transfer and competing symmetry breaking drive orbital reconstruction and emergent ferromagnetism in insulating oxide superlattices
2608.28107.summary:
- Charge transfer from NdMnO₃ to NdNiO₃ reverses Ni orbital symmetry, yielding a room‑temperature insulating state.
- Interfacial Ni²⁺–O–Mn⁴⁺ superexchange stabilizes a ferromagnetic insulating phase.
- Interface‑driven orbital reconstruction offers a pathway to spin‑insulating oxide heterostructures.

2608.28238.title: Interplay between crystal structure and magnetism in CeCrB$_4$
2608.28238.summary:
- CeCrB₄ is a ferromagnetic ground‑state metal boride with mixed‑valence Ce and charge transfer from Ce–Cr layers to B layers.
- Density‑functional GGA+U calculations reveal Cr–Cr dimers whose 3d₍z²₎ orbitals form molecular‑like bonding/antibonding states.
- The 3d₍z²₎ level splitting varies with intra‑dimer distance, mirroring classical homonuclear diatomic molecule behavior.

2608.28717.title: Charge-State Dependence of Electronic Excitations in keV Ions Transmitted Through Solids Probed by Ion-Photon Coincidence Measurements
2608.28717.summary:
- Coincidence detection of >10 eV photons from keV He ions transmitted through solids, resolving exit charge states.
- Photon yields largely material‑independent, rising steeply with ion kinetic energy, agreeing with beam‑foil excitation models.
- Validated coincidence methodology and corrections, extending the model to higher photon energies and varied materials.

2608.28719.title: Emergent hydrodynamic response and dynamical backreaction: Magnon bound-state propagation in a Bose-Hubbard fluid
2608.28719.summary:
- Examines a 1‑D Bose‑Hubbard fluid’s response to a two‑magnon bound state on an attractive XXZ chain via Holstein‑type displacement coupling.
- Derives a long‑wavelength hydrodynamic theory that predicts a comoving near‑field deformation and sound‑cone density waves, confirmed by MPS simulations.
- Finds dynamical backreaction slows the bound state and broadens its density profile, delineating the regime where hydrodynamics remains quantitatively accurate.

2608.28731.title: Statistical Properties of a Fluctuation-Driven Nanomechanical Duffing Resonator
2608.28731.summary:
- Gaussian force noise drives multiple modes of a doubly clamped nanobeam, revealing a harmonic‑to‑Duffing transition with increasing drive.
- An effective temperature, derived from fluctuation amplitude, decreases as nonlinearity dominates.
- Response statistics shift from Gaussian to platykurtic, matching Duffing‑potential predictions.

2608.28739.title: Fractal Confinement and Magnetic Self-sabotage of Current Flow: Electrons Near the Metal-insulator Crossover in a 2D $\delta$-layer
2608.28739.summary:
- Large‑scale Hartree‑Fock on 2D δ‑doped semiconductors reveals two transport regimes near a critical density.
- Conductivity rises as T drops below U₀/10, then falls at T ≈ U₀/100 when a tiny density of magnetic moments appears.
- Fractal wavefunctions amplify magnetic interactions, funneling current into filaments that are ultimately quenched by dynamic SU(symmetry breaking.

2608.28742.title: Determinant Quantum-Quantum Monte Carlo: Coherent Auxiliary-Field Sampling
2608.28742.summary:
- DQ$^2$MC replaces classical auxiliary‑field sampling with a quantum determinant oracle via singular‑value transformations, avoiding enumeration of Hubbard‑Stratonovich weights.
- Operates at the single‑particle level with only $O(\log N_{\mathrm{st}})$ qubits, eliminating fermionic encodings and Markov‑chain autocorrelation.
- Provides full‑quantum and hybrid protocols: full‑quantum removes Metropolis steps; hybrid uses constant‑size qubits, exact heat‑bath draws, and enables rejection

2608.28750.title: Floquet engineering of competing antiferromagnetism and $d$-wave superconductivity on the square lattice
2608.28750.summary:
- Floquet‑driven Lieb–Hubbard lattice yields a tunable bond attraction \(J\) in a square‑lattice spin‑½ model, independent of on‑site repulsion \(U_d\).
- In the intermediate‑coupling regime (\(J, U_d \sim t_{\text{eff}}\)), mean‑field theory finds adjacent antiferromagnetic and \(d\)-wave superconducting phases with narrow coexistence at half filling.
- The study outlines branch‑preparation, prethermal, and higher‑band conditions for implementing the

2608.28759.title: Benchtop Momentum-Resolved Phonon Spectroscopy: Unlocking Lattice Dynamics via X-ray Diffuse Scattering
2608.28759.summary:
- Benchtop SAXS/WAXS with 8 keV X‑rays captures thermal diffuse scattering in silicon, enabling extraction of interatomic force constants across the Brillouin zone.
- Global optimization of the TDS images yields fitting accuracy comparable to synchrotron‑level data.
- The method provides a low‑

2608.28831.title: Domain walls with alternating magnetic order in a model with dipolar coupling
2608.28831.summary:
- 1D chain of elongated magnetic islands with nearest‑neighbor dipolar coupling supports doubly‑degenerate transverse alternating ground states.
- Domain walls between these states broaden as the anisotropy K₁ approaches the dipolar coupling D, with continuum theory matching lattice simulations.
- A transverse applied field slightly cants dipoles, causing opposite‑sense rotation on the two sublattices across the wall.

2608.28836.title: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy of graphene nanogaps
2608.28836.summary:
- Graphene nanogaps fabricated by electrical breakdown exhibit electrochemical activity through an ultrathin conductive film at the edges.
- EIS shows Warburg diffusion behavior, with impedance systematically varying with pH, indicating edge‑reaction diffusion coupling.
- Equivalent‑circuit modeling extracts an effective nanogap length scale, complementing tunneling measurements.

2608.28848.title: Direct Evidence of Unconventional Superconductivity in Doped Kagome system RV$_3$Sb$_5$
2608.28848.summary:
- Fully gapped, two‑band superconductivity in optimally doped RbV₃Sb₅ with CDW suppressed.
- Particle‑hole asymmetric impurity‑bound states exclude conventional s‑wave and s± pairing.
- Observations match a chiral order parameter, confirming chiral superconductivity.

2608.28898.title: Phase stability, charge ordering, and charge-liquid formation in the Falicov-Kimball model on triangular and kagome lattices
2608.28898.summary:
- Spinless Falicov‑Kimball model on triangular and kagome lattices mapped with Markov‑chain Monte Carlo.
- Triangular lattice hosts Anderson, Mott, and CDW phases; a charge‑liquid regime appears between weak coupling and CDW, driven by interaction‑mediated nesting.
- Kagome lattice shows no CDW, only an insulating (likely Mott) ground state with hints of a zero‑temperature quantum transition, highlighting lattice geometry and particle‑hole symmetry effects.

2608.29062.title: Enhanced Diffusion from Twist-Angle Disorder
2608.29062.summary:
- Twist‑angle disorder in twisted bilayers acts like a curl of interlayer displacement, creating spatially correlated Hamiltonian variations.
- This geometric scattering suppresses momentum relaxation compared to white‑noise disorder, enhancing diffusion.
- The system maps onto a non‑linear sigma model, enabling quantitative analysis of transport and ordering effects.

2608.29064.title: Duality Between Twist-Angle Disorder and Non-Hermitian Disorder
2608.29064.summary:
- Twist‑angle disorder in moiré heterobilayers is modeled as a finite‑range uniform twist that randomly deforms beyond that range, with a probability distribution penalizing large deviations.
- Replica‑trick averaging yields alternating‑sign correlations between replicas, strongest near domain boundaries and along specific directions.
- A duality maps these correlations to a non‑Hermitian disorder model for fermions, showing that twist‑angle disorder can evade Anderson localization differently from conventional disorder.

2608.29089.title: Real-space manifestation of ferroic multipoles in altermagnetic MnF$_2$
2608.29089.summary:
- Polarized‑neutron diffraction maps 3D magnetization in MnF₂, isolating spherical Mn²⁺, anisotropic Mn, and F ligand spin density.
- Detects a finite F moment and Mn anisotropy consistent with the rank‑5 magnetic multipole \(O_{52}\) (triacontadipole).
- First real‑space evidence of ferroic multipolar order in an altermagnet, validating polarized‑neutron diffraction as a tool for hidden magnetic multipoles.

2608.29116.title: Electronic phase separation and emergence of a nondimerized insulating phase in VO$_2$ $(110)_{\mathit{R}}$ ultrathin films
2608.29116.summary:
- Ultrathin VO₂(films retain the temperature‑driven metal‑insulator transition down to 5 nm, but at 1 nm a nondimerized insulating phase appears.
- The nondimerized phase coexists with the dimerized phase, its fraction rising exponentially as thickness decreases, dominating at 1 nm.
- The effective critical thickness for the transition is ~2 nm, indicating that reduced dimensionality enhances Mott instability and drives the nondimerized insulating state.

2608.29142.title: Evolving charge order in the CDW state of AV$_3$Sb$_5$ metals
2608.29142.summary:
- Identified a second transition in CsV₃Sb₅ and KV₃Sb₅ below the CDW temperature, not due to magnetic fields.
- Muon‑spin spectroscopy reveals an additional charge modulation within the V plane.
- The extra charge order appears at T* < T_CDW for Cs and Rb, and near T_CDW for K.

2608.29276.title: Crystal electric field excitations and an effective-spin-$1/2$ ground doublet in the hyperkagome magnet Yb$_3$Sc$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$
2608.29276.summary:
- INS detects three dispersionless CEF excitations at ~58, 68, and 74 meV in Yb₃Sc₂Ga₃O₁₂.
- Stevens‑operator analysis (D₂ symmetry) yields an Ising‑type g tensor and a well‑isolated J_eff = ½ ground doublet ~58 meV below the first excited state.
- The revised level scheme reproduces susceptibility, magnetization, and Schottky‑anomaly data, establishing the single‑ion basis for an effective exchange Hamiltonian.

2608.29323.title: Experimental observation of decoupled spin subsystems in decorated square kagom\'{e} lattice magnets of the nabokoite family
2608.29323.summary:
- EPR detects only a fraction of Cu spins in nabokoite, revealing two decoupled spin subsystems.
- The EPR‑active spins order at the Néel temperature; the EPR‑silent spins persist as a dynamic, likely spin‑liquid component.
- Coexistence of ordered and fluctuating subsystems contradicts conventional unified exchange‑network models for decorated frustrated lattices.

2609.00070.title: AutoXRD: Autonomous LLM Agents and Comprehensive Evaluation for Powder Diffraction Analysis
2609.00070.summary:
- AutoXRD: LLM agent framework that refines powder‑XRD stepwise, grounding actions in evidence and applying crystallographic checks.
- XRDBench: 100 QA tasks + 34 end‑to‑end workflows testing reasoning, file handling, iterative refinement, and reporting.
- LLMs average 8/100; best GPT‑6 Sol scores 1; strong on refinement history, weak on action selection, phase quantification, indexing, and Rietveld refinement.

2609.00083.title: Fermi-Level Metal-d Character of Group-6 Bis-Hexahapto Bilayer Graphene
2609.00083.summary:
- Group‑6 (Cr, Mo, W) bis‑hexahapto bilayer graphene is metallic, but Fermi‑level states are ~70 % metal d rather than carbon p.
- Compared to ionic CaC₆/C₁₂Ca and C₁₂Li controls, the group‑6 systems retain only ~15–23 % interstitial spectral weight at E_F, indicating reduced carbon‑derived interlayer character.
- η₆–η₆ coordination forces AA stacking, overturning Bernal preference by 400–600 meV, and the ordered phases are metastable versus bulk metal yet bound against decomposition.

2609.00124.title: Green-function Zeros Encode Competing Mott and Charge-ordering Scales
2609.00124.summary:
- Green‑function zeros encode ordering physics in strongly correlated insulators.
- Their dispersion, set by spin correlations and defect kinematics, jumps discontinuously at the Mott–checkerboard transition.
- The effect survives further‑neighbor hopping, underscoring zero dispersion as a robust probe of competing Mott and charge‑ordering scales.

2609.00125.title: Temporal Signature of Bosonic Stimulation Induced by Dark Exciton in a Two-photon Pumped Polariton Condensate
2609.00125.summary:
- First time‑resolved evidence of dark‑exciton–induced bosonic stimulation in polariton condensates.
- Detuning‑dependent buildup/relaxation of condensate blueshifts differ between one‑ and two‑photon pumping, indicating distinct stimulation mechanisms.
- Two‑photon pumping activates a 2p‑exciton → lower‑polariton THz transition, providing a new dark‑state channel for efficient THz lasing.

2609.00139.title: Higher-Winding Fractionalization
2609.00139.summary:
- Higher‑winding skyrmions generate emergent fields with multiple flux quanta per unit cell, enabling fractionalized quantum anomalous Hall states at integer microscopic filling.
- Lattice‑scale inhomogeneity of the emergent field drives a Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition from a fractionalized liquid to a crystalline dielectric.
- The transition is topologically signaled by a quantized winding number in the many‑body polarization under flux insertion: nonzero in the liquid, zero in the crystal.

2609.00141.title: Magnetic frustration and non-collinear textures in layered Gd magnets
2609.00141.summary:
- Scale‑bridging simulations show magnetic frustration and dipolar interactions stabilize non‑collinear and skyrmion phases in GdRu₂Si₂/GdRu₂Ge₂ and related Gd layered magnets.
- Chemical tuning (e.g., alkali‑metal substitution of Gd) adjusts exchange balance and anisotropy, creating new skyrmion types stable over a wide magnetic‑field range.
- Proposed GdKRu₄Si₄ (K, Rb, Cs, Y) compounds could form ordered layered structures similar to CaKFe₄As₄,

2609.00142.title: Subgap Bound States from Dynamical Impurities
2609.00142.summary:
- A single non‑magnetic dynamical impurity (e.g., a low‑frequency vibron) creates a subgap bound state in an s‑wave superconductor.
- The bound‑state energy is given in closed form as a function of the vibron frequency in the elastic scattering limit, largely unaffected by sub‑THz inelastic processes.
- The impurity produces low‑frequency local‑density‑of‑states subgap features and spatially extended regions of reduced spectroscopic weight outside the main gap peak.

2609.00144.title: Bayesian Tracking of a Diffusing Target in Two and Three Dimensions
2609.00144.summary:
- Maps Bayesian tracking of a diffusing target to KPZ growth/directed polymer, uncovering phase structure in 2D and 3D.
- In 2D, Bayes‑optimal inference always succeeds; suboptimal overconfidence can trigger a depinning failure transition.
- In 3D, three phases appear—success, delocalized failure, and localized‑but‑wrong failure—meeting at a Nishimori‑like multicritical point, with misspecification shifting the transitions.

2609.00145.title: Size-Dependent Growth Rates Amplify Infinitesimal Asymmetry in Nanocrystals
2609.00145.summary:
- Size‑dependent nucleation barriers make facet growth rates vary with facet area, breaking symmetry even with identical microscopic laws.
- A kinetic Wulff construction that includes size dependence shows infinitesimal seed asymmetries amplify into strongly asymmetric nanocrystal shapes.
- Demonstrated on 2D lattices and 3D FCC seeds: cuboctahedra evolve into rods or tetrahedra depending on which facet‑area perturbations grow.

2609.00146.title: How Landau caterpillars turn into Hofstadter butterflies by tuning the periodic potential strength
2609.00146.summary:
- Shows how increasing periodic potential turns broadened Landau “caterpillars” into a Hofstadter butterfly, with topological transitions isolating a trivial lowest band.
- Finds the butterfly at flux φ > 1 differs from the conventional one because of anomalous diagonal hopping and flux‑dependent Wannier orbitals.
- Provides flux‑specific Wannierization and effective tight‑binding parameters, enabling accurate many‑body studies in high magnetic fields for moiré and artificial lattices.

2609.00277.title: Engineering tunable $p$-wave magnetism in antiferromagnetic bilayers
2609.00277.summary:
- In-plane shift of two AB‑stacked AFM square lattices breaks spin‑degeneracy symmetries, producing odd‑parity \(p\)-wave spin splitting without spin‑orbit coupling.
- The splitting’s magnitude and direction, and the resulting spin responses, are continuously tunable by the relative displacement of the layers.
- Mean‑field Hubbard analysis reveals extended regions of spontaneous \(p\)-wave magnetism, including coplanar and chiral spin textures, establishing a minimal 2D platform for tunable \(p\)-wave magnetism.

2609.00433.title: Bound states, resonances, and their thermodynamic properties in pseudospin-1 systems with short-range impurities
2609.00433.summary:
- Flat‑band bound states exist for all angular momenta, with energies decreasing and wavefunctions increasingly localized at the well edge as |j| grows.
- These states exhibit multicomponent pseudospin‑1 characteristics distinct from pseudospin‑½ systems, leading to unusual resonance behavior.
- In the flat‑band‑dominated regime, entropy density rises monotonically to saturation while heat capacity displays a single maximum.

2609.00697.title: Correlation-Driven Nonlinear Magnetoelectric Response in an Altermagnet: A Dynamical Mean-Field Study
2609.00697.summary:
- NMEE is finite in the altermagnetic phase, vanishes in the paramagnetic phase, and tracks the spin‑resolved spectral structure.
- At low temperature, reducing interaction strength toward the magnetic phase boundary enhances NMEE; increasing temperature suppresses it, vanishing above the critical temperature.
- The NMEE frequency dependence estimates the altermagnetic spin‑splitting scale, suggesting pressure, strain, or chemical tuning near the interaction‑driven boundary can maximize the response.

2609.01301.title: Self-Healing Diffusion Monte Carlo applied to a simple fermionic model: A critical assessment of the method
2609.01301.summary:
- SHDMC on a 1D periodic model reveals nodal dynamics as a system with attractive/repulsive fixed points.
- Standard SHDMC iterations raise fixed‑node energy and converge to an incorrect node; weighting the nodal region improves convergence.
- Complete convergence appears to need a localized basis set, as shown by this testbed.

2609.00122.title: Classification of Rational $c=1$ Vertex Operator Algebras and Vertex Operator Superalgebras
2609.00122.summary:
- Classifies all rational \(c=1\) VOAs/VOSAs as either rank‑1 lattice VOAs \(V_L\) or their finite‑group orbifolds \(V_L^G\).
- Gives a vacuum‑character criterion to detect when integer‑conformal‑dimension modules form a \(\mathrm{Rep}(G)\) fusion subcategory.
- Enumerates all admissible finite automorphism groups \(G\), yielding an explicit list of all “nice” \(c=1\) chiral algebras.

2609.00126.title: Quantum Complexity Dynamics for Disjoint Subsystems
2609.00126.summary:
- Disjoint subsystems can attain high complexity while their complement stays low, an effect that disappears at infinite temperature.
- Splitting a subsystem into \(m\) disjoint parts reduces its equilibration time by a factor of \(m\).
- Results unify holographic and random‑circuit insights, highlighting new complexity behavior beyond contiguous regions.

2609.00148.title: Regulating Free-scalar and Yang--Lee 5d CFTs on the Fuzzy Four Sphere
2609.00148.summary:
- Built 5d free‑scalar and Yang–Lee CFTs on a fuzzy 4‑sphere, finding continuous phase transition and conformal towers.
- Extracted the first three scalar primaries of the 5d free‑scalar theory.
- Computed Yang–Lee dimensions Δφ, Δφ³ with ED (Ne=and DMRG (Ne=, agreeing with ε‑expansion and bootstrap.

2609.00160.title: Exploring thermal order in conformal theories with multiple scalars coupled to an $O(N)$ vector field
2609.00160.summary: - Two Wilson–Fisher–like fixed points appear in $4-\epsilon$ dimensions for a window of $N$, with $\mathbb{Z}_2^M\rtimes S_M$ symmetry breaking at $T>0$ only for $M=2$ and

2609.01728.title: A Spatial Localizer for Constituent-Resolved Exciton Wannier Functions
2609.01728.summary:
- Introduces an exciton spatial localizer that simultaneously maximizes localization of both electron and hole coordinates using a Clifford‑algebra framework.
- Provides an ansatz‑free, gauge‑invariant construction applicable to generic multiband exciton systems.
- Demonstrates the method in an interacting bilayer model, revealing symmetry‑resolved localization of isolated exciton bands.

2609.01754.title: Phase synchronization of fish schools through spatial gaps
2609.01754.summary:
- Vision across a transparent water gap synchronizes heading of two confined fish schools.
- Each school’s center‑of‑mass shows noisy bistable dynamics, flipping between two antiparallel directions.
- Coupled stochastic bistable oscillator model quantitatively reproduces the observed phase‑synchronization.

2609.01760.title: Piston-Like Information Engine II: Boundary-Controlled Optimum in Active Matter
2609.01760.summary:
- Engine compresses self‑propelled bristle‑bot gas via measurement‑feedback, converting information into work.
- Work per measurement, \(\bar{W}\), depends on detection region size \(\Delta x\) and vacancy probability \(p_1\); deviates from thermal \(-p_1\ln p_1\) and shows two regimes as density increases.
- Regime transition arises from active particle accumulation at boundaries, also appearing in finite‑time cycles with dry friction.

2609.01805.title: Evolution from Kitaev to XXZ spin chains via distortion: Application to BaCo$_2$V$_2$O$_8$
2609.01805.summary:
- Distortions of CoO₆ octahedra produce a site‑dependent anisotropic g‑tensor and renormalize staggered exchange, partially canceling Kitaev‑derived terms.
- The combined modification of exchange interactions and g‑tensor explains the strong in‑plane critical‑field anisotropy and anomalous staggered magnetization under transverse field.
- Offers a unified microscopic framework linking spin‑orbit coupling, bond‑dependent exchanges, and lattice distortions to magnetic anisotropy in Ising‑chain antiferromagnets.

2609.01812.title: Tuning Boron-Vacancy Qubit Coherence through Layer Number in hBN
2609.01812.summary:
- T₂ grows from 199 ns (bulk) to 653 ns (monolayer), saturating at ~3 layers.
- Enhancement stems solely from boron nuclei, is independent of stacking/twist, and requires ≈

2609.01831.title: Kelvin-Helmholtz instability in annular superfluids across the UFG-BCS crossover
2609.01831.summary:
- Studied Kelvin‑Helmholtz instability in counter‑rotating annular Fermi superfluids across the UFG‑BCS crossover with time‑dependent superfluid density functional theory.
- Found a necklace of quantized vortices forms at the interface; growth rates agree with the point‑vortex model in unitary and moderate BCS regimes, largely independent of interaction strength or temperature up to ~3 Tc.
- In deep BCS regime, boundary‑generated antivortices proliferate faster than the instability, destroying the vortex necklace before full development.

2609.01844.title: Symmetry-selective nonrelativistic spin splitting in antiferromagnets driven by coherent phonons
2609.01844.summary:
- Coherent infrared‑active phonons lift spin degeneracy in collinear antiferromagnets, creating nonrelativistic spin splitting (NRSS) without magnetization.
- The symmetry of the excited phonon determines the spin‑split phase: a mode breaking all sublattice‑connecting symmetries yields an s‑wave NRSS; a mode preserving a mirror symmetry produces a d‑wave altermagnetic state.
- Spin splitting grows linearly with phonon amplitude and reverses when the lattice displacement is inverted, enabling polarization‑ and mode‑selective ultrafast control.

2609.01853.title: Magnons in Metallic Altermagnetic $\text{KV}_2\text{Se}_2\text{O}$
2609.01853.summary:
- Altermagnetic symmetry in metallic KV₂Se₂O produces directional splittings and degeneracies in both electronic bands and magnon dispersions along high‑symmetry Brillouin‑zone paths.
- Magnon linewidths arise from coupling to the particle‑hole continuum; varying the in‑plane wave‑vector direction yields pronounced angular dependence of magnon energies and lifetimes with complementary damping of the two branches.
- Spin‑orbit coupling introduces an out‑of‑plane easy‑axis anisotropy, opening a ~6 meV gap at Γ and implying room

2609.01872.title: Molecular spin qubits in a van der Waals bottle
2609.01872.summary:
- vdW confinement in SnS₂/CdPS₃ reconfigures cobaltocene’s energy landscape, cutting spin‑lattice relaxation >100×.
- Confined qubits orient deterministically and self‑assemble into atomically precise superlattices.
- Shows vdW confinement as a viable path to integrate molecular spin qubits into solid‑state quantum devices.

2609.01879.title: Morphology and Dynamics of Self-interstitial Clusters in Irradiated Nickel
2609.01879.summary: - SIA clusters in FCC Ni evolve from disordered dumbbells to either sessile Frank loops or glissile perfect prismatic loops; perfect loops

2609.01969.title: Observation of g-wave altermagnetic multipole
2609.01969.summary:
- Visualized g‑wave electric hexadecapole order in CrSb using synchrotron X‑ray diffraction and VED analysis.
- Detected coexistence of antiferroic magnetic dipoles and ferroic magnetic multipoles via polarized neutron diffraction.
- Developed a microscopic model linking g‑wave multipoles to g‑wave spin splitting, providing a real‑space fingerprint of altermagnetism.

2609.02443.title: Thermodynamic Electric Toroidal Dipole and Intrinsic Longitudinal Spin Transport
2609.02443.summary:
- Defines a gauge‑invariant thermodynamic electric toroidal dipole (ETD) as a bulk ferroaxial order parameter in periodic crystals.
- Proves that the chemical‑potential derivative of the ETD equals the intrinsic longitudinal spin conductivity, linking ferroaxial order to spin transport.
- Validates the theory with a ferroaxial Kane–Mele model, where the ETD appears only in the ferroaxial phase, is amplified near a small band gap, and drives a sizable longitudinal spin current.

2609.02466.title: Prominent Dimensional Effects on High-order Harmonic Generation in Strongly Correlated Electron Systems
2609.02466.summary:
- Dimensionality dictates HHG: 1D SrCuO₂ shows a robust plateau, weakly temperature‑dependent.
- 2D Pr₂CuO₄ yields a monotonic, thermally suppressed harmonic spectrum, especially at high orders.
- Hubbard‑model simulations attribute these contrasts to dimensionality‑dependent doublon–holon dephasing via spin–charge coupling.

2609.02506.title: Disorder-driven competing magnetic interactions and glassy magnetic behavior in quaternary Heusler alloy FeRuMnGe
2609.02506.summary:
- B2 antisite disorder (Fe–Ru, Mn–Ge mixing) in FeRuMnGe changes exchange interactions, yielding competing FM and AFM couplings and a metallic state.
- Magnetic data reveal a cluster‑glass state coexisting with long‑range order below ~161 K, with no thermodynamic signature at the freezing temperature.
- The work demonstrates that disorder‑driven exchange competition produces glassy magnetism, contrasting the AFM‑dominated FeRuMnSi with the FM‑dominated FeRuMnGe.

2609.01724.title: Bilinear correlations in Fluctuating Gaussian States with anti-unitary symmetries
2609.01724.summary:
- Introduces Fluctuating Gaussian States (FGS) with anti‑unitary symmetries, yielding positive‑definite path‑integral weights.
- Identifies two generic broken‑symmetry phases—saddle‑point and non‑local contraction—whose competition is governed by saddle‑point stability.
- Proposes a PEPS ansatz that efficiently describes the saddle‑point phase but not the non‑local contraction phase, with implications for fermionic FGS and non‑equilibrium systems.

2609.02114.title: EuIn2Sb2: epitaxially stabilized axion insulator candidate with strong spin-orbit coupling
2609.02114.summary:
- Epitaxial EuIn₂Sb₂ films exhibit a unique In‑on‑In trilayer structure distinct from prior EuA₂X₂ models.
- Displays in‑plane antiferromagnetic order at T_N = 5 K with strong spin‑orbit coupling and enhanced In‑In hybridization.
- Serves as a promising axion insulator and higher‑order topological insulator platform.

2609.02141.title: Renormalization group and long-range conditional mutual information in hierarchical models
2609.02141.summary:
- UV‑finite CMI between nonadjacent regions for states with locally reversible RG and fixed on‑site Hilbert space.
- Two hierarchical models show long‑range CMI yet simple RG flows: one diverges in Markov length yet flows to an infinite‑temperature product state; the other satisfies local but not global Markov conditions and is noise‑stable.
- At critical noise strength, two‑point CMI decays polynomially with system size while mutual information vanishes.

2609.02148.title: Charge-Transfer Electronic Structure of NiX$_2$ (X = S, Se)
2609.02148.summary:
- DFT+DMFT with tuned double‑counting reproduces valence‑band, core‑level, and XAS spectra of NiS₂.
- Charge‑transfer energy is smaller than expected, causing strong ligand‑to‑Ni transfer and a reduced Ni local moment.
- The interplay between the Ni upper Hubbard band and chalcogen‑dimer antibonding states controls the low‑energy electronic evolution across NiS₂₋ₓSeₓ.

2609.02668.title: Electronic Structure and Superconductivity in La$_{1.55}$Sr$_{0.45}$CuO$_4$/La$_2$CuO$_4$ Artificial High-$T_c$ Superlattices Probed by Hard and Soft X-ray Spectroscopy
2609.02668.summary:
- Superconducting dome in LSCO/LCO superlattices tuned by L/d ratio.
- HAXPES/XAS show chemical‑potential shift, ↑ near‑E_F weight, and enhanced local/non‑local screening.
- In‑plane orbital polarization and Fano–Feshbach resonance signatures underpin high‑T_c emergence.

2609.02933.title: Graphene-enabled dynamic H-J switching of dipole-dipole coupling
2609.02933.summary:
- Tunable graphene monolayer on metal alters dipole‑dipole coupling in H‑type/J‑type aggregates.
- Varying graphene surface conductivity shifts the parameter range where H↔J coupling inversion occurs.
- Enables real‑time observation of coupling inversion by dynamically adjusting conductivity during a single experiment.

2609.02934.title: Classical dipolar Heisenberg models on the Archimedean and Laves lattices
2609.02934.summary:
- Dipolar Heisenberg spins on 19 Archimedean/Laves lattices are solved via Fourier‑space interaction matrices, yielding Luttinger–Tisza wave vectors and ground states.
- Ground states fall into 5 collinear, 2 symmetry‑commensurate non‑collinear, and 8 transcendental‑angle canted types; incommensurate canting occurs precisely when the Luttinger–Tisza strong condition fails.

2609.02936.title: Dipolar order across Bravais lattice space: classification, spin waves, and a four-attractor phase diagram
2609.02936.summary:
- Determined dipolar ground states for all 14 Bravais lattices via Ewald‑summed tensor and Luttinger–Tisza minimization, including linear spin‑wave spectra and zero‑point corrections.
- Revealed two universal structural principles—exact tracelessness of the dipolar tensor and its vanishing at k = 0 for cubic lattices—that explain ordering types, absence of cubic anisotropy, and systematic zero‑

2609.02946.title: A Unified Description of Dirac-Cone Anisotropies in Two Dimensions
2609.02946.summary:
- Covariant Dirac‑equation extension models shifted, tilted, and distorted Dirac cones via Lorentz‑violating parameters.
- Provides a unified (2+‑D framework to systematically characterize anisotropy‑induced spectral modifications.
- Extracts effective parameters from first‑principles band structures of strained graphene, linking microscopic electronic structure to the model.

2609.02948.title: FrOGS: Discrete Neural Sampler for Independent Alloy Configurations Across Chemical Conditions
2609.02948.summary:
- FrOGS couples an autoregressive model with a continuous‑time Markov chain, trained jointly under one loss to sample alloy configurations across many chemical conditions.
- It yields unbiased partition‑function estimates and consistent thermodynamic observables, enabling free‑energy calculations on a common absolute scale without separate MCMC runs.
- Validated on 2D Ising, AgPd, and CuAu systems, FrOGS matches exact results and correctly predicts the CuAu₃ stability range, outperforming the SEGAL baseline.

2609.02957.title: Decoherence-controlled collective criticality in a two-dimensional quantum Stag Hunt
2609.02957.summary:
- Decoherence maps a two‑dimensional EWL Stag Hunt to an Ising model with channel‑dependent couplings.
- Depolarization induces an exact Ising critical point at \(p_{*}\approx233\); phase damping keeps the system ordered, confirmed by 2D Ising scaling.

2609.02960.title: Constituent-Tagged Transfer Linking Cluster Dynamics to Static Scaling
2609.02960.summary:
- Defines a conserved‑constituent exponent \(q_*\) by \(\langle(S_{t+\tau}/S_t)^{q_*}\rangle=1\), finding \(q_*\approx\alpha-2\) where \(c(s)\propto s^{-\alpha}\).
- Confirms the relation in coupled‑map networks, coagulation‑fragmentation dynamics, and Vicsek systems; radius scans recover the Vicsek interaction radius and experimental clustering scale.
- Shows local scale covariance yields the relation, while a tent‑map counterexample illustrates failure when the stationary balance is collapsed to a single moment.

2609.02966.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network Surrogate for Oxygen Vacancy Dynamics in epitaxial $\mathrm{SrTiO_3}$ on Si memristors via Dynamic Spectral Optimization
2609.02966.summary:
- Cascaded PINN with DSO V2 Hybrid spectral optimizer models ion‑electronic drift‑diffusion in Pt/SrTiO₃/Si memristors, avoiding stiffness >10¹⁶.
- Four sequential sub‑networks isolate potential, carrier density, and vacancy transport, achieving Poisson consistency and R² > 96 on conductive‑AFM I‑V hysteresis.
- Surrogate enables differentiable inverse parameter estimation and linear‑time inference, outperforming conventional FEM solvers.

2609.02968.title: Battery open-circuit voltage is not purely chemical
2609.02968.summary:
- OCV depends on mechanical state and microstructure, not only chemistry.
- Swelling‑induced particle contact generates compressive stresses that shift ion chemical potential (Hertzian scaling).
- Identical materials can show different OCV curves in different microstructures; full‑cell OCV is a chemo‑mechanical property of the entire battery.

2609.02976.title: Valley polarization dependence of candidate even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states in monolayer graphene
2609.02976.summary:
- Explored even‑denominator FQH states at ν = 1/2 and 1/4 in monolayer graphene using SU(Chern‑Simons composite‑fermion theory.
- Constructed and numerically evaluated multi‑component variational wave functions for different spin/valley polarizations in spherical geometry.
- Found that energetically favored states are multi‑component correlated liquids, distinct from a simple composite‑fermion Fermi sea, highlighting the role of valley polarization and SU(symmetry.

2609.03075.title: Orbital current rectifier and linear magnon Edelstein effect in $p$-wave antialtermagnets
2609.03075.summary:
- p‑wave antialtermagnets produce magnetization through a linear thermal Edelstein effect driven by magnon orbital moments.
- They generate perfectly nonreciprocal orbital currents via an even‑order nonlinear response, enabling orbital‑current rectification.
- Magnons in odd‑parity‑wave magnets carry no spin moment but a collinear out‑of‑plane orbital moment, linking magnonics to orbitronics.

2609.03138.title: Antiferromagnetism-altered plasmon dynamics
2609.03138.summary:
- First experimental evidence of plasmon–magnon coupling in a graphene/NiPS₃ 2D heterostructure, seen as dispersion renormalization at the antiferromagnetic transition.
- Raman and nano‑THz spectroscopy show spectral‑weight redistribution and dielectric screening changes tied to a multi‑magnon continuum.
- Establishes a platform for coherent spin‑plasmon devices in 2D materials.

2609.03271.title: Moir\'e-induced altermagnetism from nonmagnetic constituents
2609.03271.summary:
- Moiré interference between nonmagnetic layers, driven by structural relaxation and domain‑wall twirls, induces altermagnetic order.
- One electron per moiré domain opens a correlated insulating gap, with band splitting that is d‑wave or g‑wave depending on potential minima.
- d‑wave splitting is enhanced by finite twist angles, while g‑wave splitting is strain‑sensitive, allowing a transition to d‑wave.

2609.03274.title: Resolving the Magnetic Ground-State Controversy in RuO2 through A Flat Magnetic Energy Landscape
2609.03274.summary:
- RuO₂ exhibits an exceptionally flat magnetic energy landscape where nonmagnetic and multiple altermagnetic states are nearly degenerate.
- Material perturbations (e.g., defects) select the ground state mainly by altering localized Heisenberg exchange, with secondary Stoner polarization contributions.
- Spin‑orbit coupling fixes the Néel vector orientation but does not drive the emergence of long‑range magnetic order.

2609.03289.title: Symmetry-breaking line defects embedded to a 3D $O(N)$ critical bulk
2609.03289.summary:
- Stable defect CFTs found for a line defect in 3D O(N) critical bulk, with no relevant operators and lower g‑function than bulk.

- Concluded that 1D defects coupled to O(N) Wilson–Fisher bulk cannot sustain spontaneous symmetry breaking for N < 3 due to domain‑wall proliferation.

2609.03465.title: Studying line defect at Deconfined Quantum Criticality via fuzzy sphere regularization
2609.03465.summary:
- Analyzed a (0+-D pinning-field defect coupled to a (2+-D deconfined quantum critical bulk via fuzzy-sphere regularization.
- Extracted defect conformal data: scaling dimensions of defect-changing operators and the defect \(g\)-function.
- Established the first numerical characterization of line-defect conformal data at deconfined quantum criticality.

2609.03485.title: Such stuff as magic is made on: compact operator algebra, stabilizer polytope and the structure of reduced density matrices in a Kitaev spin liquid
2609.03485.summary:
- Local magic appears below a critical temperature in the Kitaev honeycomb model, captured by compact operator spaces that persist during evolution.
- Optimal magic witnesses coincide with symmetry‑resolved plaquette algebras; exact symmetry makes reduced robustness equal full robustness.
- The operator spaces form finite‑dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras, linking

2609.03513.title: Competing lattice structures induced by Sn substitution in CsV$_3$Sb$_5$
2609.03513.summary:
- Sn substitution in CsV₃Sb₅ creates local structural distortions seen in ^121Sb NQR, persisting up to x = 65 and room temperature.
- DFT predicts two nearly degenerate V‑trimer kagome structures for x = 1, differing by a zero‑ or π‑phase shift along the c‑axis.
- The work highlights a complex interplay between impurity‑induced distortions and competing lattice instabilities in kagome metals.

2609.03519.title: Non-Resonant Impulsively Stimulated Raman Scattering by a Terahertz Field: a Case Study of 1T-TaS2
2609.03519.summary:
- Non‑resonant impulsively stimulated Raman scattering via two‑photon absorption excites Raman‑active phonons in 1T‑TaS₂ with broadband and narrowband THz fields.
- Raman signatures distinctly track transitions among commensurate, nearly‑commensurate, and incommensurate CDW phases.
- Findings enable coherent control of lattice modes and cavity electrodynamic dressing using low‑energy THz radiation.

2609.04187.title: Wavefunctions for Anyon Superconductors
2609.04187.summary:
- Hierarchy‑wavefunction construction for anyon superconductors, extracting ODLRO, condensate charge, chiral central charge, and residual topological order.
- Explicit Abelian/non‑Abelian examples (semion, ν=2/3, ν=1/3, ν=1, Pfaffian); semion superconductor ↔ fermionized anyons in two Landau levels.
- Hierarchy wavefunctions emerge in the dilute limit of anyon‑Hilbert‑space theory, applicable to ideal Chern and moiré bands

2609.04164.title: A Superconducting Peierls Instability
2609.04164.summary:
- Demonstrates a superconducting Peierls instability at a 2D superconductor edge, where Bogoliubov Fermi points in a dispersing Andreev bound state generate a pairing‑mode Kohn anomaly.
- Shows that condensation of this softened pairing mode produces an edge pair‑density wave that gaps the ABS.
- Uses self‑consistent BdG calculations on a square‑lattice extended Hubbard model with mixed‑symmetry \(s+d+ip\) pairing to confirm the instability.

2609.04149.title: Non-uniform quantum geometry stabilizes generalized Wigner crystals
2609.04149.summary:
- Proposes a generalized Wigner‑crystal ansatz for Chern bands with momentum‑dependent quantum geometry.
- Compares its energy to Laughlin‑like states at ν=1/m, mapping the phase diagram versus geometric non‑uniformity.
- Shows that quantum‑geometry‑driven zero‑point charge‑density fluctuations set a Lindemann‑type criterion for crystal‑liquid transition.

2609.04146.title: HyperDet Wavefunction: A Phase-Agnostic Ansatz for Strongly Correlated Systems
2609.04146.summary:
- HyperDet wavefunction: phase‑agnostic ansatz combining parton Slater determinants via a learnable fusion tensor.
- Variational Monte Carlo yields >9 % overlap with exact ground states across bosonic and fermionic fractional Chern insulator phases.
- Bipartite fusion‑matrix singular‑value spectrum serves as a structural diagnostic, tracking phase transitions and encoding parton Chern numbers/topological data.

2609.04041.title: Cutting corners: exciting and magical bounds from the cusp bootstrap
2609.04041.summary:
- Unitarity and cutting‑gluing consistency yield bounds on cusp anomalous dimensions for conformal line defects.
- The lightest singlet cusp is always lighter than any non‑singlet for conjugate defects, forbidding level crossings as the cusp angle varies.
- An analytic “magic” functional provides an optimal universal lower

2609.04037.title: Discrete time crystals in disordered anisotropic Heisenberg chains
2609.04037.summary:
- Shows discrete time‑crystalline order in disordered anisotropic Heisenberg chains via MPS simulations.
- Observes robust subharmonic response at half the drive frequency under δ‑kick rotations, stable to small rotation errors.
- Reveals an intermediate regime with weakly correlated, Anderson‑like dynamics separating the time‑crystal and Floquet‑localized phases.

2609.04035.title: Cusped Defects: Cusp Operator Expansion, Conformal Properties and Bootstrap Applications
2609.04035.summary:
- Cusped defect scaling operators transform as primaries under conformal maps.
- Any defect shape can be expanded in a basis of cusped defects via the COE.
- Crossing equations provide analytic constraints on cusp data, opening bootstrap applications.

2609.03994.title: Evolution of electron spin resonance through a metallic quantum critical phase diagram
2609.03994.summary:
- ESR measurements across frequencies/fields reveal distinct g‑factor and linewidth behaviors in paramagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and quantum‑critical regimes of YbRh₂Si₂.
- As temperature or field approaches the quantum critical point, both g‑factor and linewidth decrease continuously, showing matching field‑ and temperature‑tuning trends.
- Findings provide experimental insight into the interplay of local moments and itinerant electrons, informing theories of ESR in strongly correlated systems.

2609.03854.title: Universal Driven Critical Dynamics of Entanglement Entropy
2609.03854.summary:
- Introduced universal finite‑time scaling for entanglement entropy, extending Kibble‑Zurek to nonlocal observables.
- Monte Carlo results for 2+1D Dirac fermions confirm corner entanglement

2609.03766.title: Ground-State Phase Diagram, Higher-Winding Topology, and Lifshitz Criticality in an Anisotropic Four-Spin XX Chain
2609.03766.summary:
- Anisotropic four‑spin XX chain in a transverse field hosts multiple gapped topological phases with winding numbers ν = 0, ±1, −2, ±3 and rich Lifshitz‑type critical boundaries.
- Lifshitz transitions arise from Fermi‑point reconstructions, including an unconventional multicritical point where distinct critical branches intersect and momentum‑space topology reorganizes.
- The ν = ±3 phases, driven by extended cluster interactions, exhibit a richer topological structure and distinct entanglement‑spectrum degeneracies compared to conventional short‑range Kitaev chains.
